disposition_reason: Text on pp. 53-54 prints lowest and highest metal values for named foods (okra, spinach, watermelon, orange) in mg/mL; full per-food results are figure-only.

study.design: market survey of two fruits and two vegetables with hazard quotients, bioaccumulation factor and pollution index
study.market: Dutse Ultra-Modern Market, Jigawa State, Nigeria (two vendors)
study.period_text: two consecutive periods within one week; dates not reported
study.method: edible parts oven dried 80 °C, microwave digestion HNO3/H2O2/HClO4 (7:2:1), AAS

findings.group: Dutse Ultra-Modern Market, two vendors, two periods within one week
findings.integrity_flag: Unit printed as mg/mL with no stated volume reference; magnitudes (for example lead 0.4-0.8 mg/mL) cannot be reconciled with a 200 mg sample in a 50 mL digest or with the conclusion that levels are within WHO limits.
findings.notes: Value printed in text as the lowest of the four foods of the four foods; per-food values for the other foods are figure-only (Figs. 1-2). Per-volume unit kept unconverted. n assumed 4 per food from 16 samples across four foods, two vendors, two periods.

unresolved: Per-food concentrations appear only as bar charts (Figs. 1-2); only the text-quoted minimum and maximum values are recorded.
The cadmium maximum (0.6±0.02 mg/mL) is printed without naming the food; not recorded.
The text says the lead hazard quotient exceeds one while Table 1 prints 0.134; unresolved.
Units mg/mL are not interpretable as concentrations in food; no conversion attempted.
Bioaccumulation factors are presented without any soil data.
